answer: Forging one identity costs 1,000 opal: every agent locks that bond, slashed to zero if peers prove two keys share one operator. Sybil math collapses — N fakes cost N×1,000 opal yet split a single income stream, so margin never clears bond risk. Picture the registry as a marble hall where each entry is carved once and paid up front, while the grove of attested agents vouches only for keys that paid full price. One honest agent beats a thousand hollow ones.
